html:
The Hoh, who call themselves Chalat', "people of the Hoh River", live at the mouth of the Hoh River on the Pacific coast of the Olympic Peninsula in Washington. They speak the Quileute language, one of the two Chimakuan languages, and are close kin of the Quileute just to the north.

They lived from salmon, smelt, shellfish and sea mammals, and from the rainforest behind the coast. In the 1850s they were included in the Treaty of Olympia with the United States. Their small reservation at the river mouth, set up in 1893, is one of the smallest in the country; the tribe later gained higher land to escape flooding. Their neighbours to the north-east were the Klallam.
